question:
In square \(ABCE,\) \(AF=2FE\) and \(CD=2DE.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle BFD\) to the area of square \(ABCE?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2008_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The sides of \(\triangle BFD\) are slanted, but the three triangles outside it have perpendicular sides along the square. Their areas are easier to calculate.

Choose \(FE\) as the length unit, so \(FE=1\). Changing the unit changes both numerical areas by the same factor and leaves their ratio unchanged. Since \(AF=2FE\), we have \(AF=2\), making each side of the square \(3\). Also, \(CD=2DE\) and \(CD+DE=CE=3\), so \(DE=1\) and \(CD=2\).

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). Using half the product of the perpendicular legs gives
\[
[ABF]=\frac{3\cdot2}{2}=3,
\qquad
[BCD]=\frac{3\cdot2}{2}=3,
\]
\[
[EFD]=\frac{1\cdot1}{2}=\frac12.
\]
These three triangles and \(\triangle BFD\) fill the square without overlapping interiors. The square has area \(3^2=9\), so
\[
[BFD]=9-3-3-\frac12=\frac52.
\]
Therefore the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{[BFD]}{\text{area of square }ABCE}
=\frac{5/2}{9}
=\boxed{\frac5{18}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
